intuition: Keep only the largest k values seen so far in a min-heap. Its smallest value is the current kth largest. A new value matters only if it is larger than that heap minimum. This avoids sorting values that cannot enter the final top k.

Use a min heap, even though the question asks for a largest rank. The root should be the weakest retained candidate, because that is the element to evict when a stronger value appears. Fill the heap until it has k values. Afterward ignore values no larger than its root and replace the root when a larger value arrives.

This preserves exactly the largest k processed values, including repeated values as separate items. The root of the final group is the kth largest: k-1 retained entries are at least as large, and every discarded entry is no larger. Distinct-value filtering would solve a different problem.
For k=1 the heap keeps only the current maximum; for k equal to input length it keeps all values and exposes the minimum.

steps: For [3,2,1,5,6,4] with k=2, insert 3 and 2; the root is 2.
Read 1. It cannot improve the retained top two, so leave the heap unchanged.
Read 5 and replace root 2. The retained values are now 3 and 5.
Read 6 and replace root 3. The retained values become 5 and 6.
Read 4 and ignore it because it is below the current weakest retained value 5.
Return heap root 5, the second-largest value.

Inductively this preserves the top collection, whose weakest member has precisely the requested rank.
